metadata.note: Command teardown of ./art keys — the dispatcher case at art:103-104 that execs runtime/scripts/check_keys.py with $@ forwarded. The Python script is 83 lines. It probes exactly one optional service (higgsfield CLI login) via `higgsfield account status` with a 25 s timeout, and writes one row into a table. Three status paths: valid (rc == 0), invalid (rc != 0, prints the failure text next to a fix line), unset (FileNotFoundError, prints 'CLI not installed'); a fourth `warn` path catches any other exception and flags the run inconclusive. Reads a repo-root .env via load_env (os.environ.setdefault, so the shell wins) but never prints a value — verified in demo/RUN-LOG.txt § 5 by grepping the output for a synthetic secret and getting zero matches. Two documentation drifts are called out honestly as the Teardown moment (B08): the docstring says 'Exit 1 if any present key is invalid' but line 40 declares any_invalid = False and never reassigns it, so exit is always 0; and the art help line at art:20 mentions 'SI key' but no SI probe exists in the script. Neither is a bug to fix in this reel — the point is that fellows should trust the live behavior, not the marketing copy. All demo output in demo/RUN-LOG.txt is verbatim from this workstation on 2026-09-09, machine higgsfield 0.2.3 installed, no active login, no .env in the toolkit tree. Playlist adaptation for @HumanitariansAI: composer folder chip reads @HumanitariansAI; outro card is the locked ClaudeTitleOutro with hardcoded @NikBearBrown handle per OUTRO-LOCK.md — flagged for the human reviewer before publication. episode.source_sha256 7c3b6abf2ec61bb70122fe12ba1e2d5bad049db19db16ddb3a1026cad274e8c6. beats.role_note: FALSIFIABILITY / the design tell — docstring promises exit 1 on invalid, code declares any_invalid=False and never reassigns it. art:20 help mentions 'SI key' but no SI probe exists. Both are honestly named; neither is fixed in this reel.
beats.narration_text: One design tell worth calling out. The docstring says exit zero if every present key is valid, one if any is invalid. Read the code. The variable any underscore invalid is declared false on line forty and never reassigned. So the invalid branch does not actually flip the exit code. And the art help line advertises an 'SI key' check — grep the script for SI, and you get zero hits. So the surface promises two things the code does not enforce. Both are harmless today — nothing in the pipeline gates on this exit — but if you ever need to fail a CI job on a red row, you now know exactly which line to patch.

show.event: card in; title reads 'the design tell — two drifts'

props.title: the design tell — two drifts
props.code:
# DRIFT 1 — the exit-code promise

# check_keys.py:8-10 (docstring):
#   "Exit 0 if every present key is valid; 1 if any present key
#    is invalid."

# check_keys.py:40 (main body):
    any_invalid = False
# …the variable is NEVER reassigned. The `invalid` branch just
# appends a red row and moves on. Exit is always 0 unless the
# probe itself throws.

# DRIFT 2 — the SI-key promise

# art:20 (dispatcher help block):
#   "./art keys   validate optional keys (Higgsfield login, SI key)"

$ grep -in 'si' runtime/scripts/check_keys.py | grep -v 'sys\|osi\|sit'
(no matches — the SI probe does not exist)

# Both drifts are harmless today. Nothing gates on this exit,
# and no build asks for an SI row. But if you ever want to fail
# CI on a red row, you now know: patch line 40 — set
# any_invalid = True inside the else branch.
props.sparkLine: Docstring promises. Code delivers one probe, exit 0.

beats.role_note: VERDICT — the whole surface, in the order you use it.
beats.narration_text: So — art keys. A live probe of one optional CLI, wrapped in a two-line dispatcher case, that prints a colored table and always exits zero. The toolkit needs no keys. This command exists so a red row is visible before you go looking for it. Run it once when you clone the repo, and run it again the day you install Higgsfield. In between, ignore it.

artifactLines: bare invocation — ./art keys; wraps runtime/scripts/check_keys.py with $@ forwarded.
one live probe — subprocess.run(['higgsfield','account','status'], timeout=25). No other service is checked.
four rows possible — valid / invalid / unset / warn. Each carries the exact message the human needs.
.env is read via setdefault (shell wins). Values are NEVER printed — verified by a redaction grep.
exit code is always 0 unless the probe itself throws. The docstring's exit-1-on-invalid contract is not enforced.
the toolkit needs no keys. Run this once at clone, and again the day you install higgsfield. In between, ignore it.
